title: Values With No Close Partner
statement:
You get two integer arrays a and b and a distance d. A value a[i] is lonely when every value in b is more than d away from it, that is |a[i] − b[j]| > d for every j.

Return how many positions of a hold a lonely value. Equal values in a at different positions are counted separately. A gap of exactly d counts as close, not lonely.

examples.why: 4 is exactly 2 away from 6, so it is close. 9 is 3 away from both 6 and 12, and 1 is 5 away from 6: both lonely.
Every 5 is 5 away from 0. The three copies count three times.
The nearest value below 7 in b is 1, far away, but 8 just above it is within 1. You must check the neighbours on both sides.

hints: For one value of a, you only care about the value of b that is nearest to it. Which values of b can be nearest?
If b is sorted, the nearest value to x is either the first value ≥ x or the last value < x.
Sort b once, then binary search each a[i]. Check the value at the insertion point and the one just before it.

explain.intuition:
A value is lonely exactly when its nearest partner in b is more than d away. So you do not need all of b for each a[i], only its nearest value.

Sorting b makes the nearest value easy to find: binary search for where a[i] would be inserted. The nearest value is either right at that spot (the first value ≥ a[i]) or just before it (the last value < a[i]). Two comparisons per value replace a full scan of b.
steps: For each x in a, binary search the first index p with b[p] ≥ x.
If p < m and b[p] − x ≤ d, x is close. If p > 0 and x − b[p − 1] ≤ d, x is close.
Otherwise count x as lonely. Return the count.
pitfalls: Checking only one neighbour of the insertion point. In a = [7], b = [1, 8] the close value is above 7, not below.
Using < d instead of ≤ d for close. A gap of exactly d is not lonely.
Forgetting the bounds: the insertion point can be 0 or m, where one of the two neighbours does not exist.

solutions.title: Compare every pair
solutions.idea: For each value of a, scan all of b and stop as soon as one value is within d.

solutions.title: Sort b, binary search each value
solutions.idea: The nearest value in sorted b sits at the insertion point or just before it. Check those two only.

followups: Sort both arrays and answer with one merge-like pass of two pointers. Why does the pointer into b never need to move back?
Instead of counting, return for each a[i] the distance to its nearest partner in b.
lcTitle: Find the Distance Value Between Two Arrays
